distinguishing_feature: Criteria: ECHO EF (HF typically shows poor LVEF; PH shows isolated RV dilation with normal LV systolic/diastolic function). Symptoms: HF features prominent orthopnea and pulmonary crackles; PH has exertional dyspnea without orthopnea/PND.
HHD driven primarily by long-standing uncontrolled hypertension without another structural cause.
SIHD chest discomfort is exertional and predictable; ACS is new worsening or occurs at rest.
Pericarditis pain is positional/pleuritic; ACS pain is typically pressure-like and exertion-related.
ACS presents with new worsening or rest symptoms; SIHD is stable and exertion-predictable.
SVT is regular and typically abrupt onset/offset; AFib is irregularly irregular.
VT is a wide-complex often hemodynamically unstable rhythm; AFib is narrow-complex and irregular.
AFib is irregularly irregular; SVT is regular with abrupt onset/offset.
VT is wide-complex and frequently unstable; SVT is narrow-complex and usually stable.
Bradyarrhythmia has abnormally slow rate; VT has abnormally fast rate - opposite ends of the rhythm spectrum.
AS murmur is systolic ejection radiates to carotids; MR is holosystolic radiates to axilla.
MR murmur is holosystolic radiating to axilla; AS murmur is systolic ejection radiating to carotids.
Myocarditis has recent viral illness and acute onset; cardiomyopathy is typically more gradual or has a family/toxin history.
Pericarditis pain is positional/pleuritic; myocarditis pain is less positional and paired with arrhythmia/heart-failure signs.
Pericarditis pain worsens lying flat and improves leaning forward; ACS pain is typically pressure-like unaffected by position.
PE has sudden onset and usually unilateral leg swelling; HF has gradual onset and typically bilateral edema.

Criteria: ECHO EF (PH shows isolated RV dilation with normal LV systolic/diastolic function; HF typically shows poor LVEF). Symptoms: PH has exertional dyspnea without orthopnea/PND; HF features prominent orthopnea and pulmonary crackles.
HHD is driven primarily by chronic hypertension; HF may have multiple structural causes and more pronounced congestive symptoms.
